questions.q: For what reason did the people of Moab, Ammon, and the Meunites come against Jehoshaphat?
questions.a: They came against Jehoshaphat to do battle.

questions.q: Where did the people of Judah come from to seek Yahweh?
questions.a: The people came to seek Yahweh from all the cities of Judah.

questions.q: Where did Jehoshaphat stand in the assembly of the people?
questions.a: Jehoshaphat stood at the house of Yahweh, in front of the new courtyard.

questions.q: What promise of Yahweh did Jehoshaphat repeat when the people cried to him in their affliction?
questions.a: Jehoshaphat said that when the people cry to Yahweh in their affliction, he would hear them and save them.

questions.q: What did Yahweh not let Israel do to Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir when they came out of Egypt?
questions.a: Yahweh would not let Israel invade them when they came out of the land of Egypt.

questions.q: What part of the people of Judah stood before Yahweh?
questions.a: All Judah stood before Yahweh, with their little ones, wives, and children.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh say not to fear or be discouraged by the great army against them?
questions.a: Yahweh told them not to fear or be discouraged because of this great army, for the battle did not belong to them, but to God.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say the people would see when they stood still in their positions?
questions.a: Yahweh told them to stand still, and see the rescue of Yahweh with them.

questions.q: What did Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem do in worship before Yahweh?
questions.a: All Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before Yahweh, worshiping him.

questions.q: As the army went out, why did Jehoshaphat say to give thanks to Yahweh?
questions.a: As they went out preceding the army, Jehoshaphat told them to say, “Give thanks to Yahweh; for his covenant faithfulness endures forever.”

questions.q: What did Yahweh do when the people of Judah began to sing and praise?
questions.a: When they began to sing and praise, Yahweh set men in ambush against their enemies.

questions.q: What did the people of Judah see when they looked out on the enemy’s army?
questions.a: When they looked out on the army, they were dead, fallen to the ground.

questions.q: How long did it take the people to carry off the plunder from the army?
questions.a: It took the people three days to carry off the plunder, because there was so much of it.

questions.q: Why did Jehoshophat and his people return to Jerusalem with joy?
questions.a: They returned to Jerusalem with joy for Yahweh had made them rejoice over their enemies.

questions.q: What did God give Jehoshaphat that made his kingdom quiet?
questions.a: Jehoshaphat’s kingdom was quiet, for his God gave him peace all around him.

questions.q: What had Jehoshaphat done in the eyes of Yahweh?
questions.a: Jehoshaphat did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh.

questions.q: What was prophesied against Jehoshaphat, because he allied himself with Ahaziah?
questions.a: Because Jehoshaphat had allied himself with Ahaziah, Yahweh destroyed his projects.

commentary.text: The danger and distress of Judah.

Verses 1–13 In all dangers, public or personal, our first business should be to seek help from God. Hence the advantage of days for national fasting and prayer. From the first to the last of our seeking the Lord, we must approach him with humiliation for our sins, trusting only in his mercy and power. Jehoshaphat acknowledges the sovereign dominion of the Divine Providence. Lord, exert it on our behalf. Whom should we seek to, whom should we trust to for relief, but the God we have chosen and served. Those that use what they have for God, may comfortably hope he will secure it to them. Every true believer is a son of Abraham, a friend of God; with such the everlasting covenant is established, to such every promise belongs. We are assured of God's love, by his dwelling in human nature in the person of the Saviour. Jehoshaphat mentions the temple, as a token of God's favourable presence. He pleads the injustice of his enemies. We may well appeal to God against those that render us evil for good. Though he had a great army, he said, We have no might without thee; we rely upon thee.

The Spirit of prophecy came upon a Levite in the midst of the congregation. The Spirit, like the wind, blows where and on whom He listeth. He encouraged them to trust in God. Let the Christian soldier go out against his spiritual enemies, and the God of peace will make him more than a conqueror. Our trials will prove our gain. The advantage will be all our own, but the whole glory must be given to God.

Jehoshaphat exhorted his troops to firm faith in God. Faith inspires a man with true courage; nor will any thing help more to the establishing of the heart in shaking times, than a firm belief of the power, and mercy, and promise of God. In all our trust in the Lord, and our praises of him, let us especially look at his everlasting mercy to sinners through Jesus Christ. Never was an army so destroyed as that of the enemy. Thus God often makes wicked people destroy one another. And never was a victory celebrated with more solemn thanksgivings.

Jehoshaphat kept close to the worship of God, and did what he could to keep his people close to it. But after God had done such great things for him, given him not only victory, but wealth; after this, to go and join himself with a wicked king, was very ungrateful. What could he expect but that God would be angry with him? Yet it seems, he took the warning; for when Ahaziah afterward pressed him to join him, he would not, 1Ki 22:49. Thus the alliance was broken, and the Divine rebuke had its effect, at least for a season. Let us be thankful for any losses which may have prevented the loss of our immortal souls. Let us praise the Lord, who sought after us, and left us not to perish in our sins.
